title: Continuously-stirred Anaerobic Digester to Convert Organic Wastes into Biogas: System Setup and Basic Operation
protocol: Select a digester vessel with desired working volume between 1-10 L.
Place the digester in a heated water bath or incubation chamber if not equipped with a heated-water jacket.
Secure the digester vessel in a vertical position on the bench.
Construct the vessel lid according to Fig. 2 specifications.
Ensure ports of influent and effluent tubes are wide enough to prevent clogging.
Insert tubes inside the bioreactor, ensuring they stay submerged during decanting while extending out for tubing attachment.
Extend impeller sheathing as far as possible into the digester medium to prevent headspace biogas from escaping.
Apply silicone-based vacuum grease to the lid's contact surface.
Clamp the vessel lid securely onto the digester vessel top.
Secure the variable speed mixer parallel to the digester’s vertical axis using a ring-stand and clamps.
Affix impeller shaft to the mixer.
Use an independent and free-moving stand for the mixer to counteract motor vibrations and movement.
Connect a section of flexible tubing to both the influent and effluent tubes.
Connect another section of tubing to the gas port to be used as the gas line.
Connect the biogas line to the sampling port.
Connect the biogas line to the foam trap.
Connect the biogas line to the H2S scrubber.
Connect the biogas line to the gas reservoir.
Connect the biogas line to the bubbler.
Connect the biogas line to the gas meter.
Connect the biogas line to the ventilation line.
Add valves and connector fittings between components for isolation or removal purposes.
Position the gas sampling port near the reactor headspace.
Construct the foam trap using a simple flask or bottle, at least 25% of the reactor volume.
Drill two holes in a rubber stopper through which rigid tubing is inserted for ports on the foam trap.
Extend the biogas inlet tube to a greater depth than the biogas outlet tube.
Prepare the H2S scrubber using a long glass tube filled with steel wool and connected biogas inlet and outlet ports.
Pack the steel wool well but not too tightly in the glass tube.
Ensure the gas reservoir is made from an air-tight, collapsible material exceeding twice the targeted feed volume.
If temperature control is required, connect the heater to the heating jacket using flexible tubing.
Place the unit above the liquid level of the heating jacket.
Set the heater to the appropriate temperature for mesophilic or thermophilic digestion.
Perform a leak test by filling the digester tank with water and slightly pressurizing the influent line.
Check for leaks around the reactor lid first, then remove the biogas line clamp to check the entire gas handling system.
Turn on the impeller and heating element and let run overnight.
Ensure the rotational speed of the impeller is sufficient for complete mixing.
Store the active methanogenic biomass in a closed container at 4 °C.
Dilute the inoculum with anaerobic-flushed water to the appropriate volume if necessary.
Flush the empty digester system with an anaerobic gas for several minutes.
Connect a funnel to the feeding tube after flushing is complete.
Add the diluted inoculum into the digester, mixing periodically.
Reconnect the anaerobic gas to the feeding tube.
Turn on the mixer.
Flush the digester liquor for at least 15 minutes.
Disconnect the gas.
Clamp the feed tube.
Unclamp the gas reservoir.
Monitor the production of biogas.
Perform total solids and volatile solids concentration analysis for the inoculum.
If the solids concentration is greater than the target mixed liquor concentration, remove and dilute digester contents accordingly.

Determine the organic biodegradable fraction of the substrate by measuring either the total and volatile solids concentration, biological or chemical oxygen demand, or total organic carbon of the substrate.
Calculate a conservative initial organic loading rate (OLR).
Gradually increase the OLR until a target value is reached during the start-up period.
Fix the organic strength of the feed initially.
Reduce the hydraulic retention time incrementally until the target OLR is achieved.
Monitor volatile fatty acid concentrations; reduce OLR if concentrations exceed suboptimum levels.
Dilute bioreactor contents with water if volatile fatty acid concentrations are too high.
Allow a period of three HRTs at the target OLR before experimentation to establish stable conditions.
Prepare the feed mixture immediately before decanting effluent from the digester.
Store the prepared feed mixture at 4 °C until it is time to add it to the digester.
Decant effluent from the digester by connecting the effluent tubing to a pump.
Remove an equal volume of effluent compared to the feed volume.
Store the effluent at 4 °C for later analysis.
Remove the feed mixture from the refrigerator.
Connect a funnel to the feed tube.
Pour in the feed (substrate).
Mix periodically to ensure solids get carried with the fluid.
Check the digester system and its components frequently during operation.
Pay particular attention to the mixing and heating systems.
Measure the biogas production rate every feeding cycle.
Measure the pH immediately after each feeding cycle.
Measure the volatile fatty acid concentration multiple times a week.
Measure the alkalinity multiple times a week.
Measure the biogas content multiple times a week.
Sample the biogas at the end of a feeding cycle, just prior to feeding.
Measure the biological oxygen demand once a week or more often.
Measure the chemical oxygen demand once a week or more often.
Measure the total solids once a week or more often.
Measure the volatile solids once a week or more often.
Verify that the pH is within the optimal range for methanogenesis (i.e., 6.5 to 8.2).
Supplement with acidity or alkalinity if the pH is outside this range.
Check for leaks near the sampling port if significant nitrogen is detected in the biogas (>10%).
Regularize the periodicity of biogas sampling.
Verify that the VFA concentration is within the optimal range.
Reduce the OLR if the VFA concentration is chronically high.
Supplement nutrients or trace metals if deficiencies are present.
Verify that the reactor contents are sealed from oxygen intrusion.
Increase feed cycle frequency if necessary.
Eliminate hydraulic short circuiting to improve reactor performance.
Supplement alkalinity if there is a deficiency.
